record.original_question: Let P be a univariate polynomial of degree d >= 2, and for integers n >= 1 and 0 <= m <= nd define Q_{n,m}(x) = d^m(P(x)^n)/dx^m. Let Upsilon_P be the closure of the union of all roots of all Q_{n,m}(x). If the roots of P are in convex position but do not form a regular polygon, must Upsilon_P be a closed domain inside the convex hull of the roots of P, with all critical points of P on the boundary of Upsilon_P, no inflection points on that boundary, and boundary contained in the union of the critical values, with respect to z, of F_alpha(z) = z - alpha P(z)/P'(z) as alpha ranges over [0,d]?

evidence.quote: Consider the double-indexed polynomial family Qn,m(x) = d^m P^n(x) / dx^m, where 0 <= m <= nd. Obviously, for any pair of non-negative integers (n, m), all roots of Qn,m(x) lie in the convex hull of the roots of P(x). Consider the union of all roots of all Qn,m(x) with 0 <= m <= nd and denote the closure of the latter countable set as Upsilon_P - the shadow of the polynomial P(z).

Conjecture 1. For any polynomial P of degree at least 3 whose roots are in convex position, but do not form a regular polygon, (i) Upsilon_P is a closed domain in the convex hull of the roots of P. (ii) All critical points of P lie on the boundary of Upsilon_P. (iii) the boundary of Upsilon_P has no inflection points. (iv) The boundary of Upsilon_P is contained in the union of all critical values (w.r.t. z) of the rational function F_alpha(z) = z - alpha P(z)/P'(z), where the parameter alpha runs over the interval [0, d].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P(z)$ be a univariate complex polynomial of degree $d\ge 3$ whose roots are in convex position in $\mathbb{C}$ (i.e., they are the vertices of a convex polygon) but do not form the vertices of a regular polygon. For nonnegative integers $n\ge 1$ and $0\le m\le nd$, define
\[ Q_{n,m}(x) \;=\; \frac{d^{m}}{dx^{m}}\bigl(P(x)^{n}\bigr). \]
By the Gauss–Lucas theorem, all roots of each $Q_{n,m}$ lie in the convex hull of the roots of $P$. Define the shadow of $P$ to be
\[ \Upsilon_P \;=\; \overline{\bigcup_{n\ge 1}\;\bigcup_{0\le m\le nd}\{\,x\in\mathbb{C}\,:\,Q_{n,m}(x)=0\,\}}. \]
For a parameter $\alpha\in[0,d]$, consider the rational function
\[ F_\alpha(z) \;=\; z - \alpha\,\frac{P(z)}{P'(z)}. \]
Prove or disprove the following statements:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\Upsilon_P$ is a closed domain contained in the convex hull of the roots of $P$.
\item[(ii)] Every critical point of $P$ (i.e., every root of $P'$) lies on the boundary $\partial\Upsilon_P$.
\item[(iii)] The boundary $\partial\Upsilon_P$ has no inflection points.
\item[(iv)] $\partial\Upsilon_P$ is contained in the union, over $\alpha\in[0,d]$, of the critical values (with respect to $z$) of $F_\alpha$.
\end{enumerate}

artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is stated in a 2023 open-problems collection from the Hausdorff Geometry of Polynomials workshop and in a related manuscript "Shadows of Polynomials and Gauss–Lucas Theorem" by Shapiro and collaborators. No published proof or counterexample of the four-part conjecture appears in the literature; it remains an open conjecture.
